memory_update.text: Add SYY and USFD as core upstream food-input and distribution candidates for the franchisee unit-economics node; both can indicate restaurant customer health, food-cost pressure, and procurement scale advantages.
Add TOST as the strongest public restaurant operating-system candidate for digital throughput, payments, labor, guest engagement, and productivity tooling tied to franchisee ROIC.
Add MIDD and ITW as equipment and kitchen-infrastructure candidates tied to new-unit capex, remodel economics, automation, service reliability, and energy/labor efficiency.

Below-USD-1B or near-threshold restaurant-tech names such as PAR and NCR Voyix may be highly relevant to enterprise restaurant POS, labor, inventory, and back-office systems, but were excluded from the top-five list due to market-cap preference and weaker balance of scale/purity.

Need a later pass for construction/remodel suppliers, HVAC/refrigeration service providers, restaurant real estate landlords, delivery aggregators, and franchisee financing providers, which are adjacent but outside this focused supplier/equipment pass.

node: Franchisee unit economics and new-unit development
summary: This pass expands the universe around second-order suppliers and infrastructure vendors that can influence franchisee ROIC, new-unit build costs, operating labor intensity, food-input availability, and digital throughput. The highest-relevance public-market exposures are not more restaurant brands, but foodservice distributors, restaurant operating-system software, and commercial kitchen equipment vendors whose products can affect food cost, labor scheduling, order capture, throughput, maintenance burden, and buildout/remodel economics.
